instructions: Shred the cheddar on the large holes of a box grater.
Cut the 4 tbsp cold butter into small cubes.
Put the cheddar, butter, 1 cup flour, 1/2 tsp ground mustard and 3/4 tsp salt in a food processor. Pulse until it looks like coarse crumbs.
With the processor pulsing, add 2 tbsp cold water a little at a time, until the dough starts to clump together.
Turn it out onto plastic wrap, press it into a ball and wrap it tightly. Chill it in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350°F and line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.
Roll the dough out on a clean counter into a thin rectangle about 1/8 inch thick.
Cut it into 1 inch strips with a pizza cutter, then cut across the strips to make squares.
Poke a hole in the middle of each square with a toothpick or the tip of a knife.
Set the squares on the baking sheets close together, without touching.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes, until they're puffed, crisp and golden at the edges. This makes 6 snack servings.
Let them cool completely on the sheets, then keep them in an airtight container. If they go soft, warm them in the oven for a few minutes to crisp them again.
method_notes: All four work 8 oz of sharp cheddar into about 1 cup flour, 4 tbsp butter and salt with a little cold water, chill the dough, roll it 1/8 inch thick and cut 1 inch squares. Bee Yond Cereal (the lead, since none of the pages has 20 ratings) does it in a food processor with ground mustard, chills it 20 minutes and bakes at 350°F for 13 to 15 minutes. The Decorated Cookie and 4 Sons R Us use a stand mixer, chill an hour and bake at 375°F, and Little House Living chills an hour or more. This follows the lead as written.
